items.stem: For how many integers n does the inequality |4n-9|<7 hold?
items.explanation: Rewrite the absolute-value inequality as -7<4n-9<7. Adding 9 and dividing by 4 gives 1/2<n<4. The integers strictly between 1/2 and 4 are 1, 2, and 3, so there are 3 such integers.
items.pattern: count integers strictly inside an interval

per_choice.correct: Rewrite the absolute-value inequality as -7<4n-9<7. Adding 9 and dividing by 4 gives 1/2
per_choice.trap: A student may count the length of the interval, 4-1/2=3.5, instead of counting integer locations, or may incorrectly include n=4 even though the inequality is strict.

items.stem: In the figure shown, what is the distance between the two points?
items.explanation: Distance on a number line is the absolute value of the difference of the coordinates: |2 - (-5)| = 7.

items.explanation: The interval extends from -4 to 2, so its midpoint is -1 and its radius is 3. Because both endpoints are open, the inequality is |x + 1| < 3.

items.stem: For the equation |3x + 1| = 10, what is the product of the 2 solutions for x?
items.explanation: Split the equation into 3x + 1 = 10 and 3x + 1 = -10, giving x = 3 and x = -11/3. Their product is 3*(-11/3) = -11.

per_choice.correct: Split the equation into 3x + 1 = 10 and 3x + 1 = -10, giving x = 3 and x = -11/3. Their product is 3*(-11/3) = -11.
per_choice.trap: The choice 13 results from ignoring the negative sign, -10 results from omitting the +1 when solving the negative branch, and -2/3 results from adding the solutions instead of multiplying them.

items.trap: The choice 13 results from ignoring the negative sign, -10 results from omitting the +1 when solving the negative branch, and -2/3 results from adding the solutions instead of multiplying them.

items.stem: The graph of y=abs(x-3)-4 crosses the horizontal axis at which of the following x-values?
items.explanation: At an x-intercept, y=0. Thus abs(x-3)-4=0, so abs(x-3)=4. Therefore x-3=4 or x-3=-4, giving x=7 or x=-1.
items.pattern: read all zeros from absolute-value graph

per_choice.correct: At an x-intercept, y=0. Thus abs(x-3)-4=0, so abs(x-3)=4. Therefore x-3=4 or x-3=-4, giving x=7 or x=-1.
per_choice.trap: 3 is the vertex of the graph, not an x-intercept. Reporting only -1 or only 7 also misses one of the two places where the graph crosses the horizontal axis.

items.stem: For all real numbers x satisfying |x - 4| + |x + 2| = 10, what is the product of all possible values of x?
items.explanation: The two fixed points are -2 and 4, whose distance is 6, so x must lie outside the interval between them for the sum of distances to be 10. Solving on the two outside regions gives x = -4 and x = 6, whose product is -24.

per_choice.correct: The two fixed points are -2 and 4, whose distance is 6, so x must lie outside the interval between them for the sum of distances to be 10. Solving on the two outside regions gives x = -4 and x = 6, whose product is -24.
per_choice.trap: Choosing 24 results from taking the absolute value of the product; choosing -4 or 6 results from finding only one of the two solutions.

items.stem: A delivery drone can be at position t on a straight path. Its distance from a station at position -7 is twice its distance from a station at position 1. What is the sum of all possible values of t?
items.explanation: The condition is |t + 7| = 2|t - 1|, so the two cases are t + 7 = 2(t - 1) and t + 7 = -2(t - 1). These give t = 9 and t = -5/3, whose sum is 22/3.

per_choice.correct: The condition is |t + 7| = 2|t - 1|, so the two cases are t + 7 = 2(t - 1) and t + 7 = -2(t - 1). These give t = 9 and t = -5/3, whose sum is 22/3.
per_choice.trap: Choosing 9 or -5/3 results from solving only one absolute-value case; choosing 32/3 results from subtracting the two solutions instead of adding them.

items.trap: Choosing 9 or -5/3 results from solving only one absolute-value case; choosing 32/3 results from subtracting the two solutions instead of adding them.

items.stimulus: For all real numbers x such that |2x - 3| <= |x + 4|, which of the following must be true?
items.explanation: Both sides are nonnegative, so squaring preserves the inequality: (2x - 3)^2 <= (x + 4)^2. Factoring gives (x - 7)(3x + 1) <= 0, so -1/3 <= x <= 7; statements I and II must be true, but III fails at x = 7.

per_choice.correct: Both sides are nonnegative, so squaring preserves the inequality: (2x - 3)^2 <= (x + 4)^2. Factoring gives (x - 7)(3x + 1) <= 0, so -1/3 <= x <= 7; statements I and II must be true, but III fails at x = 7.
per_choice.trap: Squaring incorrectly, reversing the inequality when factoring, or checking x^2 <= 16 only at the left endpoint instead of testing the full interval.

items.trap: Squaring incorrectly, reversing the inequality when factoring, or checking x^2 <= 16 only at the left endpoint instead of testing the full interval.

items.stimulus: For all real numbers x such that |x - 3| <= 2|x + 1|, which of the following must be true?
items.explanation: Squaring both nonnegative sides gives (x - 3)^2 <= 4(x + 1)^2, or 3x^2 + 14x - 5 >= 0. The roots are -5 and 1/3, so x <= -5 or x >= 1/3; this makes both I and II true, while III fails for x < -5.

per_choice.correct: Squaring both nonnegative sides gives (x - 3)^2 <= 4(x + 1)^2, or 3x^2 + 14x - 5 >= 0. The roots are -5 and 1/3, so x <= -5 or x >= 1/3; this makes both I and II true, while III fails for x < -5.
per_choice.trap: Discarding the negative solution interval after finding the roots leads to III or to an incomplete version of I; forgetting that the quadratic is nonnegative outside its roots reverses the solution intervals.

items.trap: Discarding the negative solution interval after finding the roots leads to III or to an incomplete version of I; forgetting that the quadratic is nonnegative outside its roots reverses the solution intervals.

items.stem: For the real number x such that ||x - 2| - 3| = 1 and -1 < x < 2, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: The outer absolute value gives |x - 2| - 3 = 1 or |x - 2| - 3 = -1, so |x - 2| = 4 or 2. The resulting solutions are -2, 0, 4, and 6, and only 0 satisfies -1 < x < 2.

per_choice.correct: The outer absolute value gives |x - 2| - 3 = 1 or |x - 2| - 3 = -1, so |x - 2| = 4 or 2. The resulting solutions are -2, 0, 4, and 6, and only 0 satisfies -1 < x < 2.
per_choice.trap: Ignoring the interval restriction produces one of the other solutions of the absolute-value equation, such as -2, 4, or 6.

items.trap: Ignoring the interval restriction produces one of the other solutions of the absolute-value equation, such as -2, 4, or 6.

items.stimulus: For all real numbers x such that |x - 2| <= 5 and |x + 1| > 2, which of the following must be true?
items.explanation: The first inequality gives -3 <= x <= 7, while the second gives x < -3 or x > 1; together these reduce the solution set to 1 < x <= 7. Thus I and II are always true, but III fails when x = 7.

per_choice.correct: The first inequality gives -3 <= x <= 7, while the second gives x < -3 or x > 1; together these reduce the solution set to 1 < x <= 7. Thus I and II are always true, but III fails when x = 7.
per_choice.trap: Replacing the strict inequality |x + 1| > 2 with a non-strict one incorrectly includes x = 1, or overlooking the endpoint x = 7 can make III appear true.

items.trap: Replacing the strict inequality |x + 1| > 2 with a non-strict one incorrectly includes x = 1, or overlooking the endpoint x = 7 can make III appear true.

items.stem: For a real number x satisfying |x - 3| + |x + 5| = 16 and |x + 1| > |x - 4|, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: The first equation has solutions x = -9 and x = 7, found by considering the regions x <= -5 and x >= 3. The inequality selects x = 7 because |7 + 1| = 8 > 3 = |7 - 4|, whereas x = -9 does not satisfy it.

per_choice.correct: The first equation has solutions x = -9 and x = 7, found by considering the regions x <= -5 and x >= 3. The inequality selects x = 7 because |7 + 1| = 8 > 3 = |7 - 4|, whereas x = -9 does not satisfy it.
per_choice.trap: A student may find both solutions to the absolute-value equation but fail to apply the second condition, choosing -9; sign errors when solving the left branch can produce -7 or 9.

items.trap: A student may find both solutions to the absolute-value equation but fail to apply the second condition, choosing -9; sign errors when solving the left branch can produce -7 or 9.

items.stimulus: The figure shows the set S. If x is any number in S, which of the following statements must be true?
items.explanation: Every number in the open interval from -4 to 2 is between -5 and 4 after adding 1, and the isolated points -6 and 4 also satisfy |x + 1| <= 5. Completing the square gives x^2 + 2x <= 24 as (x + 1)^2 <= 25, while x = -6 disproves III.

per_choice.correct: Every number in the open interval from -4 to 2 is between -5 and 4 after adding 1, and the isolated points -6 and 4 also satisfy |x + 1| <= 5. Completing the square gives x^2 + 2x <= 24 as (x + 1)^2 <= 25, while x = -6 disproves III.
per_choice.trap: Ignoring the isolated point at -6 can lead to choosing III only or treating all three statements as true; failing to complete the square can make II appear unrelated to I.

items.stimulus: For a real number x such that |x - 2| = |3x + 4|, which of the following statements must be true?
items.explanation: Squaring both sides gives (x - 2)^2 = (3x + 4)^2, which simplifies to 2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0, so III must be true. The two solutions are -3 and -1/2, making x < 0 true and x > -3 false.

per_choice.correct: Squaring both sides gives (x - 2)^2 = (3x + 4)^2, which simplifies to 2x^2 + 7x + 3 = 0, so III must be true. The two solutions are -3 and -1/2, making x < 0 true and x > -3 false.
per_choice.trap: Using only x - 2 = 3x + 4 captures x = -3 but misses x = -1/2; using only x - 2 = -(3x + 4) captures the other branch and can incorrectly make II appear necessary.
